title: Understanding the Anesthesiologists Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion with Casual Loading and Super
description: Convert an anesthesiologists salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks. Includes casual loading, super, tax, and Fair Work Commission rates for 2026.
salarySummary: Based on ABS data, the median full-time anaesthetist earns $8,293 per week (46 hours), which equates to roughly $431,236 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, $50 per hour × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect the super guarantee calculation?
faqs.a: Yes. Super is calculated on ordinary time earnings, which for casual employees includes the 25% loading. So if your casual rate is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 + 25% loading), super is 12% of that loaded rate, not just the base. The super is paid on top of the gross pay.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 and how does it compare to an anesthesiologists salary?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1004.90 per week. Casual employees get 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. An anesthesiologists median hourly rate is much higher, around $180 per hour, but award-covered workers must receive at least the minimum.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay: The 38-Hour Week and the National Minimum Wage

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the simplest conversion is: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 ordinary hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This article explains how to calculate annual pay, including casual loading and super, and uses the **anesthesiologists salary** as a high-earning example to illustrate the process.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay (before tax) = hourly rate × weekly hours × 52. If you work exactly 38 hours each week, the formula becomes: hourly × 38 × 52. For instance, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, giving $1004.90 per week, and $52,254.80 annually. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides full details.

If you are a casual employee, a 25% casual loading applies on top of the base rate. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) explains the loading is added to the hourly rate, not included in the rate you type. The calculator on the [timesheet](/).

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the gross pay. For casual employees, the 25% loading is part of ordinary time earnings, so the super is calculated on the loaded rate. For example, the casual rate $33.05 per hour (including loading) gives $1,256.90 per week, and super is 12% of that, not just the base. The maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per year (2026-27).

### Anesthesiologists Salary: A Real-World Example

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data from Jobs and Skills Australia, the median full-time anaesthetist earns $8,293 per week (based on 46 hours average). The Australian spelling is anaesthetist, but the keyword **anesthesiologists salary** is used here. Using the standard 38-hour week for conversion, the hourly rate would be $8,293 ÷ 46 = $180.28 per hour. Then annual salary (38-hour week) would be $180.28 × 38 × 52 = $356,000 approximately. However, if you use the actual 46 hours, annual is $8,293 × 52 = $431,236. The difference highlights why you should use your actual hours, not the standard week.

### Award Rates and Award-Free Employees

Most employees are covered by a modern award set minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database provides detailed rates for each award. For award-free employees, the National Minimum Wage applies. The Fair Work Commission's National Minimum Wage page confirms $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Casual loading is 25% on top of that.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

After calculating gross annual pay, you can estimate tax using the 2026-27 resident tax scale: nil to $18,200; 15% to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 38% above. Medicare levy is generally 2% (with reduction thresholds from 2025-26 used here). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help.

### Fortnightly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage, fortnightly is $2,009.80. For the anesthesiologists salary example, fortnightly would be $16,586 (based on $8,293 per week).

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

To convert hourly to annual, use: hourly × hours per week × 52. For casual workers, add 25% loading. Super is paid on top. The anesthesiologists salary example shows how actual hours can differ from the 38-hour standard. Always check your award or agreement. Use the [reference tables](/data) for more data.
